content_units: One-Day Festival Game Plan
Here’s the best-fit schedule based on your priorities:   synthwave, art pop, indie rock, and alt R&B  , while avoiding an exhausting run of peak-energy sets and leaving room for a proper food break.
Recommended Set Schedule
Time   Artist   Genre   Length   Energy   Why it makes the cut
13:00   Circuit Choir   synthwave   50m   3   Direct hit on your top genre priority; great early momentum without burning energy too soon.
14:15   Marble Foxes   indie rock   60m   4   Another top-priority genre, placed well after Circuit Choir for a strong afternoon peak.
15:45   Nia Vale   alt R&B   45m   2   Gives you one of your preferred genres while intentionally lowering intensity after Marble Foxes.
16:45   Copper Avenue   folk-pop   40m   1   Best built-in chill window for food, sitting, and recharging before the evening lift.
19:00   Saffron Echo   art pop   50m   3   Essential pick from your stated priorities; a smart re-entry point after the break.
20:15   Midnight Reverie   electronic   75m   4   Strong finale with danceable energy, but not a back-to-back energy-5 overload.
Why This Flow Works
-   All four of your priority genres are covered
- synthwave:   Circuit Choir
- indie rock:   Marble Foxes
- alt R&B:   Nia Vale
- art pop:   Saffron Echo
-   No back-to-back highest-energy acts
- The only energy-5 set is   Voltage Kids  , and this schedule skips it.
- That avoids a late-day spike that could make the evening feel too relentless.
-   A real food-break set is built in
-   Copper Avenue   at energy 1 is the best slot to eat, sit down, hydrate, and reset.
- It also creates a nice pacing arc before the stronger evening finish.
-   The day rises and falls naturally
- Start with moderate excitement.
- Hit a strong early peak with   Marble Foxes  .
- Come down with   Nia Vale   and   Copper Avenue  .
- Rebuild with   Saffron Echo  .
- End with   Midnight Reverie   for a satisfying close.
Best Alternative if You Want More Chaos Late
Option 1: Swap   Midnight Reverie   for   Voltage Kids     Bigger adrenaline finish, but less aligned with your genre priorities   Highest-energy ending
Use alt ending
Why you might choose it:
- Pick this only if you want your finale to feel louder and more explosive.
- It’s fun, but it sacrifices some fit versus your stated preference for   art pop / synthwave / indie rock / alt R&B  .
Option 2: Add   Aurora Lane   at 12:00   Softer opening if you want a fuller day   Gentle warm-up
Add opener
Why you might choose it:
- Good if you enjoy easing in early rather than arriving at 13:00.
- It’s pleasant, but not as important as your higher-priority genres.
Quick Actions
Save schedule
Set reminders
Lineup Notes
Brief planning context: this recommendation assumes you want a   balanced, enjoyable full-day path  , not simply to maximize the number of sets.
-   Skipped Aurora Lane   because it’s a nice opener, but not one of your top genres.
-   Skipped Voltage Kids   because although it could be exciting, it is   energy 5   and less aligned with your core preferences than   Saffron Echo   or   Midnight Reverie  .
-   Kept Copper Avenue   even though folk-pop is not a priority, because it solves your “chill set for food break” requirement better than any other option.
